title: Regularization of an embedded curve by point blowups
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $Y\subseteq X$ be an integral closed subscheme of dimension $1$. Suppose the normalization of $Y$ in its function field is finite. There exists a finite sequence $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ of blowups at reduced closed points such that the successive strict transform $Y_n$ is regular. Each centre can be chosen to be a singular closed point of the current strict transform of $Y$. Conventions: [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-sc-normalization], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-strict-transform], [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Stacks Project Tags 0BI4 (resolve-lemma-resolve-curve) and 0BI5 (resolve-lemma-blowup-curve): factor the finite normalization resolution through point blowups and use strict-transform compatibility.

proof.text: First $Y$ is Noetherian. Take a finite affine open cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ of $X$ by Noetherian rings. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], its inverse images in $Y$ are affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/J_j)$, and they cover $Y$. Each quotient is Noetherian: the preimage in $A_j$ of any ideal of $A_j/J_j$ has finitely many generators by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and their images generate the quotient ideal. This is a finite affine Noetherian cover of $Y$, so $Y$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0BI5, hypotheses: the closed curve in the Noetherian ambient scheme

proof.text:
Put $N=Y^
u$ and write $
u:N	o Y$. By [lem-per-finite-curve-normalization-regular], $N$ is an integral Noetherian regular curve and $
u$ is finite and birational. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent], the module $\mathcal M=
u_*\mathcal O_N$ is coherent on the Noetherian scheme $Y$. The parenthetical structure-sheaf case of that node applies directly; no excellence or field-of-definition assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0BI4, proof: start from the finite normalization resolution

proof.text: Construct an intrinsic tower starting at $C_0=Y$ with $r_0=\nu:N\to C_0$. Maintain that $C_i$ is an integral Noetherian curve, $r_i$ is finite and birational, and $f_i:C_i\to Y$ is finite and birational with $f_ir_i=\nu$. If $C_i$ is not regular, choose a singular point $c_i$. It is closed: on an integral one-dimensional scheme every nongeneric point is closed, and the generic local ring is a field and hence regular. Apply [lem-per-singular-curve-point-blowup-step] to $(C_i,N,r_i,c_i)$. This produces the nonisomorphic finite birational blowup $b_i:C_{i+1}\to C_i$ and the finite birational factor $r_{i+1}$. Set $f_{i+1}=f_ib_i$. Finiteness of the composite can also be checked directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: on an affine of $Y$, the two inverse images are affine, and products of finite module generators for the two successive ring extensions generate the composite. The generic field maps compose to an isomorphism. Thus the invariant holds at the next stage.

source.place: Tag 0BI4, proof: inductive construction of the factorizations

proof.text: For each stage regard $\mathcal A_i=f_{i,*}\mathcal O_{C_i}$ as a submodule of $\mathcal M$ using $r_i$. Indeed, on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$, finiteness identifies $f_i^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $\nu^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}D$; the ring maps $A\to B_i\to D$ are injections because all schemes are integral and all maps induce isomorphisms of function fields. Compatibility $b_ir_{i+1}=r_i$ gives $\mathcal A_i\subseteq\mathcal A_{i+1}\subseteq\mathcal M$. Each $\mathcal A_i$ is coherent, hence quasi-coherent, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] applied to $f_i$. If adjacent submodules were equal, the induced map $B_i\to B_{i+1}$ would be an isomorphism on every affine open of $Y$. Taking spectra gives that $b_i$ is an isomorphism, contrary to its construction. Thus every step made while singular gives a strict inclusion. These are affine ring identifications using the definition of a finite morphism, rather than a claim that arbitrary scheme morphisms are detected by their global functions.

source.place: Tag 0BI4, proof: the increasing sequence of coherent submodules

proof.text: If no stage were regular, the preceding recursive construction would give an infinite strictly increasing sequence $\mathcal A_0\subsetneq\mathcal A_1\subsetneq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal M$ of quasi-coherent submodules of a coherent module on the fixed Noetherian scheme $Y$. This contradicts [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent]. Hence it stops at some finite $n$ with $C_n$ regular. If $Y$ was regular initially, take $n=0$. This proves termination of the intrinsic construction, including its choice of singular reduced point at each nontrivial step.

source.place: Tag 0BI4, proof: stabilization by coherent.tex Tag 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent)

proof.text: Lift this finite tower to the ambient scheme by induction. Start with $X_0=X$ and the given closed immersion $C_0=Y\hookrightarrow X_0$. Suppose $X_i$ is Noetherian and $C_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ is a closed immersion. The reduced point $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c_i)\hookrightarrow C_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], so its image is closed in $X_i$. Its ideal is of finite type, since ideals on Noetherian affine opens are finitely generated. Blow up this reduced closed point to obtain $X_{i+1}\to X_i$. This blowup is proper by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; consequently $X_{i+1}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The point centre is also finitely presented: on any affine its quotient algebra has finitely many defining ideal generators. The extended centre ideal on $C_i$ is exactly $\mathcal I_{c_i}$: on a local affine presentation $A\twoheadrightarrow B=A/J$ with point ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $J$, the extended ideal is $\mathfrak m B=\mathfrak m/J$, the ideal of that same reduced point on $C_i$. By [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup], the strict transform is therefore canonically $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_{c_i}}C_i=C_{i+1}$. By [def-nagata-strict-transform] it is closed in $C_i\times_{X_i}X_{i+1}$; the latter is closed in $X_{i+1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Composition of these closed immersions again uses [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. This establishes the induction with the requisite scheme structures, not merely equality of underlying point sets.

source.place: Tag 0BI5 (resolve-lemma-blowup-curve), proof: lift the intrinsic point blowups using strict-transform compatibility

proof.text: The resulting successive strict transform $Y_n\subseteq X_n$ is isomorphic to the regular curve $C_n$. Every chosen ambient centre is the reduced closed point $c_i$, which was singular on the current transform $C_i$. The finite ambient tower therefore has both asserted properties; the empty tower covers the initially regular case.
